# Background & aims

1.  

# Setup

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(glmmTMB)
library(easystats)
library(broom.mixed)

data_traits_climate <-
  arrow::read_parquet("data-processed/data_traits_climate.parquet") |>
  select(decimal_longitude:life_stage, growth_form_simpler, life_history, woody) |>
  mutate(
    log_annual_precipitation = log(annual_precipitation),
    log_value = log(value)
  ) |>
  # Let's also collect the mean rainfall and temp for each species, and devitations of each from their respective mean
  group_by(taxon_name) |>
  mutate(
    log_annual_precipitation_mn = mean(log_annual_precipitation),
    log_annual_precipitation_c = log_annual_precipitation - log_annual_precipitation_mn,
    average_temperature_mn = mean(average_temperature),
    average_temperature_c = average_temperature - average_temperature_mn
  ) |>
  ungroup()

data_traits_climate_woody <- data_traits_climate |>
  filter(woody == "woody")
```

# Comapring two methods: Straight Mixed effects models vs Cornwell-Ackerly Method

Let's try within species for LMA

```{r}
trait <- "leaf_mass_per_area"

data_model <- data_traits_climate_woody |>
  filter(trait_name == trait)

fit0 <- glmmTMB(log_value ~ log_annual_precipitation, data = data_model)
fit1 <- glmmTMB(log_value ~ log_annual_precipitation + (1 | taxon_name), data = data_model)
fit2 <- glmmTMB(log_value ~ log_annual_precipitation + (log_annual_precipitation | taxon_name), data = data_model)

# strong support for random intercepts and slopes by species
anova(fit0, fit1, fit2)

# plot fitted lines
data_fit <- estimate_expectation(fit2) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(across(c("log_annual_precipitation", "Predicted"), exp))

data_fit |>
  ggplot(aes(log_annual_precipitation, Predicted, group = taxon_name)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(y = trait, x = "annual rainfall")
```

Looks promising. But....

Note, as a LMM, the species slope is the combination of the fixed effect and random effects. The random slopes themselves are centered around zero, as their mdoelled as deviations from the fixed effect slope.

The fixed slope is 

```{r}
parameters(fit2)
```

and the random slopes

```{r}
random_slopes <-
  broom.mixed::tidy(fit2, effects = "ran_vals") |>
  filter(term == "log_annual_precipitation") |>
  select(level, estimate) |>
  rename(taxon_name = level, random_slope = estimate)

random_slopes |>
  ggplot(aes(random_slope)) +
  geom_histogram()
```


One might initially think the fixed effect slope is the average slope within species, but that would be a mistake. It would be if all species occurred across the gradient and we had samples from all species.  But the distribution of species along the gradient is unequal. As you move from left to right, the mean trait value for species enteringis lower than species leaving. In other words, the fixed effect slope includes two biological effects added together:

1. The average slope within  species
2. Shifts in the trait means of species along the gradient. 

We see the problem if we plot, if we fit the mixed model after first standardizing the data around each species' average rainfall. 

```{r}
# Fit cenetred model
fit2_c <- glmmTMB(log_value_c ~ log_annual_precipitation_c + (log_annual_precipitation_c | taxon_name), data = data_model)

# plot fitted lines
data_fit_c <- estimate_expectation(fit2_c) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(across(c("log_annual_precipitation_c", "Predicted"), exp))

data_fit_c |>
  ggplot(aes(log_annual_precipitation_c, Predicted, group = taxon_name)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.2) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(y = "Leaf mass per area (centered)", x = "annual rainfall (cenetered)")
```

Not, quite variable, but lots of values close to zero and 95% of values lie within [-0.616 to 0.622]

```{r}
random_slopes_fit2_c <- broom.mixed::tidy(fit2_c, effects = "ran_vals") |>
  filter(term == "log_annual_precipitation_c") |>
  select(level, estimate) |>
  rename(taxon_name = level, random_slope = estimate)

random_slopes_fit2_c$random_slope |>
  stats::quantile(probs = c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975))
```

The overall fixed effect (average response within species) is -0.17 [-0.22, -0.12]

```{r}
parameters(fit2_c)
```

In an ideal mixed model setup, centering the data shouldn't change the slopes within species. But here it is. Whereas previosuly the fixed slope was -0.42 [-0.45, -0.38], it's now -0.17 [-0.22, -0.12]


So what we need to do is seperate out the effect of within species variation from species turnover along the gradient. What we implement below is similar to what was proosed by Cornwwll and Ackerly 2009, who seperated trait change along a graident into different components. 

We can do this by fitting two different models:

1. A Mixed Effects Model calculated where the x variables are centered around the species mean (i.e. as we did above.). This will enable us to capture the average species within species response to variation in the environmental variable and individual species deviations from that overall mean. 
2. A model fitted through the bivariate means of species trait and climate, i.e. values at the center of its distribution. This will capture the tendency for average trait values for species to change with environment.

Let's build th model

We already have part 1 (fit2_c), so we need part 2.   To estimate the trait value at the center of a species distribution, we can use the original mixed model with random slopes and intercepts by species, i.e. fit2.  

Let's caluclate predictions at the center of each species x (log_annual_precipitation_mn):
```{r}
data_centers <- data_model |>
  select(taxon_name, log_annual_precipitation = log_annual_precipitation_mn) |>
  distinct() |>
  filter(!is.na(log_annual_precipitation))

pred_centers <- estimate_expectation(fit2, data_centers) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  rename(log_value = Predicted)

# model across species means
fit4 <- glmmTMB(log_value ~ log_annual_precipitation, data = pred_centers)

parameters(fit4)
```

The slope of this model is -0.59, which is steeper than the slope in the original mixed model (-0.42). 

So what we have is

- Slope of mean trait with mean climate = -0.59 [-0.62, -0.56]
```{r}
parameters(fit4)
```

- Average slope of within species response to climate =  -0.17 [-0.22, -0.12]

```{r}
parameters(fit2_c)

```

- Slope of naive linear mixed effect model -0.42  [-0.45, -0.38]

```{r}
parameters(fit2)
```


Let's plot the results from the centered model

```{r}
data_fit4 <- estimate_expectation(fit4, data = pred_centers |> select(taxon_name, log_annual_precipitation)) |>
  as_tibble()

p_fit <-
  pred_centers |>
  ggplot(aes(log_annual_precipitation, log_value)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line(data = data_fit4, aes(y = Predicted)) +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(y = trait, x = "log annual rainfall")

p_fit
```

What about adding on the within species variation

```{r}
data_fit2_c <-
  estimate_expectation(fit2_c) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  arrange(taxon_name)

data_fit_all <-
  data_fit2_c |>
  select(log_annual_precipitation_c, taxon_name, Predicted) |>
  left_join(
    by = "taxon_name",
    pred_centers |> arrange(taxon_name) |> select(taxon_name, log_annual_precipitation, log_value)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    log_annual_precipitation_mn = log_annual_precipitation,
    log_annual_precipitation = log_annual_precipitation_mn + log_annual_precipitation_c,
    log_value_mn = log_value,
    log_value = log_value_mn + Predicted,
    annual_precipitation = exp(log_annual_precipitation),
    annual_precipitation_mn = exp(log_annual_precipitation_mn),
    value = exp(log_value)
  )

a <- fit4_coefs$Coefficient[1]
b <- fit4_coefs$Coefficient[2]

taxa <- data_model |>
  group_by(taxon_name) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    n_x = n_distinct(annual_precipitation)
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(n > 4, n_x > 4) |>
  pull(taxon_name) |>
  unique() |>
  sample(30)

data_model_taxa <- data_model |>
  filter(taxon_name %in% taxa) |>
  mutate(taxon2 = taxon_name)

data_fit_taxa <- data_fit_all |>
  filter(taxon_name %in% taxa) |>
  mutate(taxon2 = taxon_name)

p_fit <-
  data_fit_all |>
  ggplot(aes(annual_precipitation, value, group = taxon_name)) +
  # raw data
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, col = "grey", data = data_model, stroke = 0) +
  # fitted lines
  geom_line(alpha = 0.5, col = "black", linewidth = 0.25) +
  # highlight certain species
  geom_point(aes(group = taxon2), col = "orange", show.legend = FALSE, data = data_model_taxa, size = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(x = annual_precipitation_mn, y = exp(log_value_mn), group = taxon2), alpha = 0.5, data = data_fit_taxa, col = "red") +
  geom_line(aes(group = taxon2), col = "orange", alpha = 1, show.legend = FALSE, data = data_fit_taxa) +
  geom_line(data = data_fit4 |> mutate(annual_precipitation = exp(log_annual_precipitation), value = exp(Predicted), taxon_name = "average"), col = "red") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(y = trait, x = "annual rainfall") +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~taxon2)

ggsave("multiplot_fitted2.png", p_fit)

# p_fit

```

# new approach - a single model

```{r}
# model across species means
fit5 <- glmmTMB(log_value ~ log_annual_precipitation_mn + log_annual_precipitation_c + (log_annual_precipitation_c | taxon_name), data = data_model)

parameters(fit5)

data_fit5 <- estimate_expectation(fit5) |>
  as_tibble()

data_fit5_global <- estimate_means(fit5, by = "log_annual_precipitation_mn") |>
  as_tibble() |>
  select(log_annual_precipitation = log_annual_precipitation_mn, log_value = Mean) |>
  mutate(
    annual_precipitation = exp(log_annual_precipitation),
    value = exp(log_value),
    taxon_name = "average"
  )

data_fit5_mn <- estimate_expectation(fit5,
  data = data_fit5 |> mutate(log_annual_precipitation_c = 0) |> select(-Predicted) |> distinct()
) |>
  as_tibble()

data_fit5_all <-
  data_fit5 |>
  rename(log_value = Predicted) |>
  select(-SE, -Residuals) |>
  left_join(
    by = c("log_annual_precipitation_mn", "taxon_name"),
    data_fit5_mn |> select(log_annual_precipitation_mn, taxon_name, log_value_mn = Predicted)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    log_annual_precipitation = log_annual_precipitation_mn + log_annual_precipitation_c,
    annual_precipitation = exp(log_annual_precipitation),
    annual_precipitation_mn = exp(log_annual_precipitation_mn),
    value = exp(log_value),
    value_mn = exp(log_value_mn),
  )


data_fit5_taxa <- data_fit5_all |>
  filter(taxon_name %in% taxa) |>
  mutate(taxon2 = taxon_name)

p_fit <-
  data_fit5_all |>
  ggplot(aes(annual_precipitation, value, group = taxon_name)) +
  # raw data
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, col = "grey", data = data_model, stroke = 0) +
  # fitted lines
  geom_line(alpha = 0.5, col = "black", linewidth = 0.25) +
  # highlight certain species
  geom_point(aes(group = taxon2), col = "orange", show.legend = FALSE, data = data_model_taxa, size = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(x = annual_precipitation_mn, y = value_mn, group = taxon2), alpha = 0.5, data = data_fit5_taxa, col = "red") +
  geom_line(aes(group = taxon2), col = "orange", alpha = 1, show.legend = FALSE, data = data_fit5_taxa) +
  geom_line(data = data_fit5_global, col = "red") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(y = trait, x = "annual rainfall") +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~taxon2)

ggsave("multiplot_fitted3.png", p_fit)
```

## Compare two methods

Compare species slopes in 2 methods

```{r}
# Centered version
species_slopes_c <-
  broom.mixed::tidy(fit2, effects = "ran_vals") |>
  filter(term == "log_annual_precipitation_c") |>
  select(level, estimate) |>
  rename(taxon_name = level, slope_c = estimate)

# non-centered version
B_fixed <- parameters(fit3) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  filter(Parameter == "log_annual_precipitation") |>
  pull(Coefficient)

species_slopes_r <-
  broom.mixed::tidy(fit3, effects = "ran_vals") |>
  filter(term == "log_annual_precipitation") |>
  select(level, estimate) |>
  rename(taxon_name = level, slope_r = estimate) |>
  mutate(slope_r = slope_r + B_fixed)

species_slopes <- left_join(species_slopes_r, species_slopes_c)

p <- ggplot(species_slopes, aes(slope_c, slope_r)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", col = "red")
ggsave("tmp.png", p)
```

Fixed effects:  Average fixed effect slopes differ a lot

```{r}
# In pooled model -- slope = 1.28
parameters(fit0)

# In random effects model - slope = 0.51
parameters(fit3)

# Across species means -- slope = 1.64
parameters(fit4)

# Range of within species slopes - mean slope = -0.06 ([-0.20, 0.09])
parameters(fit2)

stats::quantile(species_slopes_c$slope_c, probs = c(0.05, 0.5, 0.9))
```
